page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 84 at upper left. Above the text, a list of numbered items (CIX–CXIV) in full width. Below, main text in one column with a large woodcut initial C, with marginal notes in the left margin beside the paragraph (Gregorius VII, Sub quatuor Pontificibus, Daemoniacis artibus). Final line "nis" at lower right, continuing the paragraph.

main_text.l: CIX. Pontificum erga Monachos mendicantes favor. Guilhelmi de S. Amore adversus eos liber.
CX. Monachorum æternum Euangelium meditantium horribilis conatus eodem libro detectus.
CXI. Et à Pontificibus segniter repressus.
CXII. Euangelium illud æternum blasphemiis refertum horum & sequentium temporum nudum Papatum repræsentare, ostenditur.
CXIII. Alexandri IV. Urbani IV. Clementis IV. Gregorii X. Nicolai III. Honorii IV. &c. historia. Rodolphus Imp. Romam ire detrectat, & Papam bolo Romandiolæ donatæ placat.
CXIV. Mænardi Comitis Tirolensis oratio adversus effæminatos Antichristos & prodigiosos Eunuchos acris.
main_text.p: LXXIX. Gregorius VII. Sede Pontificia rapta strenuè Papatum provexit. Umprimis verò Papatus Gregorii VII. Hildebrandi vulgò dicti, Pontificium Regnum, depressa Majestate Imperatoria, ad ἀρχὴν strenuè perduxit. Erat Hildebrandus ille natione Hetrufcus, Sena oriundus, professione Cluniacensis Monachus. Papatum A. MLXXIII. spreta authoritate Imperatoris, contemptóque Cleri & populi suffragio, vi remotis, qui obstare improbis conatibus viderentur, rapiens, abusus eam in rem pupillari ætate Henrici III. juxta quosdam IV. Imperatoris, qui quinquennis tum sub tutela matris Agnetis educabatur. Sub quatuor Pontificibus Dominus Papa cluebat. Jam ante sub quatuor Pontificibus, Pontificiis artibus assuetus, earúmque callentissimus, plus quàm Papam se gessit, adeò ut eum Petrus Damiani Dominum Papæ appellaverit, eíque dicere non erubuerit:

l.i: Papam rite colo, sed te prostratus adoro,
Tu facis hunc dominum, te facit ipse Deum.

main_text.p: Daemoniacis artibus im- Ejus adventum fuisse ex operatione Sathanæ, insignis

page.notes: Left margin notes are partly cut off at the edge; marginal note text transcribed as legible. The line ending "nis" is a catchword-like continuation at the lower right and is kept as the paragraph end. Line "Daemoniacis artibus im-" is a marginal note, rendered as printed.
